constraints.implication: GS-R1 GPU arms are compile-bound streaming lanes: at GPU scale the batched tape collapses toward zero cost, but per-genome encode (morphology.compile.compile_genome, CPU-only, irreducible while #71 forbids learned components inside OCM organisms) becomes ~78% of lane cost. GPU throughput therefore scales with CPU encode parallelism feeding the device, not with kernel efficiency; lane sizing should budget encode cores >= device count.

fidelity_claim_scope.claim: exact-equality fidelity (not correlation) on the measured sample
fidelity_claim_scope.exact_statement: On the measured sample (n=120 census-grammar draws, seed 2210, billy-laptop py3.8.10) the batched T0 tape reproduced evaluate_genome('T0') with 0 dev_score mismatches and Spearman 1.0 vs the per-organism exact path; numpy-vs-py backend identity max_abs_diff 0.0. The tape transcribes the same frozen arithmetic (elementwise fp64, round only at assembly), so identity is by construction — but the EMPIRICAL claim is scoped to this sample and to the field-sweep + random-sample suites in tests/test_gs_gpu_laptops.py (13/13 green on py3.8.10 and py3.14.4), NOT a proof over all grammatically reachable genomes.

amend_5_carry_in.admission_bar: GS arms must declare admission bars PROSPECTIVELY; the amend-5 quality gate carries in: seed-mean own_axis_recovery >= 0.224507 and junk_free_ratio == 1.0 asserted per task
amend_5_carry_in.census_ceiling_semantics: census maxima are census-SUBSET maxima, not bounds on the mutated space — mutations draw from full vocabularies, so a GS arm must never clamp or normalize against census maxima as if they were space bounds
